rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete transition-and-savings template: it establishes a cutoff date, then uses a sequence of provisos to preserve specified pre-cutoff rights or proceedings while limiting post-cutoff consequences. The child follows the same drafting architecture for the new courts-martial manual, with an effective date followed by successive provisos preserving pending proceedings, barring retroactive punishment, and preserving earlier punishment ceilings. C06 shares the successive-proviso form and a maximum-limit clause, but its compensation rules are less structurally analogous. C10 contains isolated savings language amid unrelated substantive regulations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: on and after February 1, 1949 ... Provided, that nothing contained in this manual shall be construed to invalidate any investigation, trial ... or other action begun prior to February 1, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall expire on October 22, 1948, unless application ... shall have been made before that date: Provided, that nothing in this order shall prevent the exercise of such reemployment rights on or after October 22, 1948
shared_material.explanation: Both establish a date-based transition and immediately preserve specified rights or proceedings connected to the earlier regime.
The child reproduces the parent's cascading proviso structure to state multiple transition safeguards.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the maximum punishment for an offense committed prior to February 1, 1949, shall not exceed the applicable limit in effect at the time
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any person who subsequent to October 22, 1948, takes any action ... may not exercise such reemployment rights
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the transition provision by limiting the legal consequences attached to conduct occurring on one side of the cutoff date.
